Thanks — reviewed and attached a short redline (see comments). High-level notes and proposed language below.

1) Scheduled Maintenance / Exclusions
Proposed text (legal-friendly):
"Scheduled Maintenance" means Provider-initiated, pre-announced maintenance that is reasonably expected to interrupt Service. Provider shall provide at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice for Scheduled Maintenance and shall not schedule more than four (4) hours of Scheduled Maintenance in any calendar month. Scheduled Maintenance shall be excluded from the calculation of Availability.

Provider and Customer may agree to two (2) planned maintenance windows per quarter that may exceed the monthly cap; such exceptions must be documented in an agreed change order.

2) Availability measurement
Proposed text:
"Availability" shall be calculated over a rolling thirty (30) day period by default. Availability = (Total Minutes in the rolling 30-day period - Minutes of Downtime - Minutes of Scheduled Maintenance) / (Total Minutes in the rolling 30-day period). Partial-minute downtime shall be rounded up to the nearest minute for calculation purposes.

If Customer requires a calendar-month measurement instead of rolling 30-day, Customer shall select that option in the Order Form.

3) Service Credit Matrix and cap
Proposed matrix (legal & commercial compromise):
- Availability >= 99.90%: No credit
- Availability >= 99.50% and < 99.90%: 10% credit of the Monthly Fee
- Availability >= 99.00% and < 99.50%: 25% credit of the Monthly Fee
- Availability < 99.00%: 50% credit of the Monthly Fee
Credits shall be the sole and exclusive remedy for Availability failures and shall be capped at fifty percent (50%) of the Monthly Fee for the month in which the failure occurs. Credits shall be applied to the following month's invoice.

4) Response times / severity definitions
Proposed:
- P1 (Service Down / Production outage impacting all users): Initial response within 1 hour; target remediation SLT depends on incident but will be tracked in incident report.
- P2 (Partial outage / severe degradation): Initial response within 4 hours.
- P3 (Minor impact): Initial response within 24 hours.

5) Emergency maintenance
Emergency maintenance required to address a critical security vulnerability or imminent risk to availability may be performed with as much notice as practicable. Emergency maintenance will be documented and shall not be considered Scheduled Maintenance for the purpose of Availability calculations, but Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize customer impact.

Please confirm ops feasibility on the 4 hour/month cap and the rolling 30-day default. If Ops pushes back on 4 hours, we should be ready to offer 4 hours as standard with a one-time quarterly exception process.

Happy to finalize language and send back to Acme.

Regards,

Samantha — thanks for the redlines and for your patience while we reviewed internally. Below is the consolidated counter-proposal; please confirm whether Acme can accept, or highlight any remaining non-starters. If accepted, we'll prepare a short amendment and send via DocuSign.

Summary of counter-proposal (high level):
- Scheduled Maintenance: Provider to provide >= 72 hours' notice; standard cap of 4 hours per calendar month; two planned windows per quarter may exceed cap with documented change order.
- Availability measurement: Default = rolling 30-day window; calendar month measurement available if selected in Order Form. Partial minutes rounded up.
- Service credits: tiered matrix (>=99.90% no credit; 99.50-99.90% = 10%; 99.00-99.49% = 25%; <99.00% = 50%), credits capped at 50% of monthly fee and applied to next invoice; credits are sole remedy.
- Response times: P1 initial response 1 hour; P2 initial response 4 hours; P3 initial response 24 hours.
- Emergency maintenance: excluded from Scheduled Maintenance but will be documented and minimized; no routine credits for emergency maintenance when required to mitigate security risks.
